name_zh: 玻利维亚·埃沃·莫拉莱斯：可可原住民总统与气候海洋权利
name_en: Bolivia Evo Morales: Coca Indigenous President & Climate Ocean Rights
description_zh: 埃沃·莫拉莱斯 (1959-) 玻利维亚首位原住民总统 (2006-2019)，可可种植合法化捍卫原住民文化，多民族国家宪法确立自治权，气候正义主张海洋出路权，2019年政变流亡墨西哥回归。
description_en: Evo Morales (1959-) Bolivia first indigenous President (2006-2019), coca legalization defended indigenous culture, plurinational constitution established autonomy rights, climate justice claimed ocean access right, 2019 coup exiled Mexico returned.
reason_zh: 莫拉莱斯代表原住民如何通过选举政治夺取国家权力并重写宪法，展示了可可文化权利与气候正义如何超越单一民族国家框架，其政变流亡与回归折射玻利维亚种族阶级博弈的深度。
reason_en: Morales represents how indigenous people seized state power through electoral politics and rewrote constitution, demonstrating how coca cultural rights and climate justice transcend mono-ethnic nation-state framework, his coup exile and return reflecting Bolivia racial-class struggle depth.
steps_zh: 研究莫拉莱斯早年可可农民与工会领袖崛起
分析2009年多民族国家宪法与原住民自治权
探讨可可合法化与单一公约条款冲突博弈
评估气候正义海洋出路权与智利领土争端
总结可可原住民总统气候海洋权利对拉美原住民政治的里程碑意义
steps_en: Study Morales early coca farmer and union leader rise
Analyze 2009 plurinational constitution and indigenous autonomy rights
Explore coca legalization and Single Convention clause conflict game
Evaluate climate justice ocean access right and Chile territorial dispute
Summarize coca indigenous president climate ocean rights milestone for Latin American indigenous politics
expected_zh: 掌握原住民选举夺权如何重写国家契约，理解可可文化权利与气候正义双重超越西方法律框架的逻辑，评估莫拉莱斯模式对厄瓜多尔秘鲁等安第斯原住民运动的示范。
expected_en: Master how indigenous electoral seizure rewrites national contract, grasp coca cultural rights and climate justice dual transcendence of Western legal frameworks, evaluate Morales model demonstration for Ecuador Peru Andean indigenous movements.
case_zh: 2006 总统；2009 宪法；2019 政变流亡；2020 回归。可可原住民总统气候海洋权利范式永存。
case_en: 2006 President; 2009 Constitution; 2019 coup exile; 2020 return. Coca indigenous president climate ocean rights paradigm endures.
intellectual_tradition: Andean Indigenous Politics / Plurinationalism / Climate Justice
cross_cultural_impact: Indigenous presidency; plurinational constitution; coca rights; climate justice; ocean access
